rationale: M59 (#825). Every line below is read off lines-825.groovy. Before this round the groovy analyzer emitted NO line at all on any relationship (measured: 0 of 761 on a 40-file sample) and every symbol range started at the declaration's leading ANNOTATION — the pinned grammar gives `@Deprecated\nclass Wrapped` children `[modifiers@18, identifier@19, class_body@19]`, so a tool navigating to Wrapped opened `@Deprecated`. Pins: the class at 19 and its members at 23/26 (annotations on 22/25 skipped, including their `contains` and `overrides` edges); each heritage parent on its OWN line (`extends Plain` 19, `implements Marker, Second` both 20); a same-line member read at 27; the type in a declared-type reference at 23; and both continuation calls of a chain at the CALLEE's own line (29, 30) rather than the receiver's 28 — the scala defect, re-checked on groovy's own node shape. The forbid entries are the positions a naive implementation produces: the annotation line, the class header line for a second parent, and the chain-opening line. Deliberately NOT pinned HERE: a newline-continued PROPERTY read (`this\n  .label`), which the pinned grammar shapes as `leading_dot_call` and which used to fabricate a `calls` edge to the property. That defect (and its dotted-juxt sibling) is fixed and has its own fixture with its own one-line controls — `groovy/continuation-shapes-851` (M49 W20, issues #851/#852) — so this file keeps pinning only the line contract, deliberately not duplicating the edge-set contract.
